title: Me Without You
full_review:
Writer-director Sandra Goldbacher explores the joys and perils of extremely close female friendships in the disquieting drama "Me Without You" (IDP).

Set in London and covering a time period from the 1970s to the present, "Me Without You" is an aptly titled film which chronicles the turbulent friendship between Holly (Michelle Williams) and Marina (Anna Friel), best friends since childhood. The film is a study of a consuming relationship between co-dependent opposites which captures the difficulties that can disrupt even a close female relationship. But while the characterizations are authentic and the performances compelling, viewers may be troubled by the casual representation of sexual encounters and drug use.

Holly is a studious and sensitive girl from a reserved Jewish family while Marina is self-centered, wild, and conniving. Her parents are morally bankrupt. Yet these two females find in each other tremendous solace from their individual loneliness. So close are they as children that they decide to combine their names into Harina, symbolically linking their identities. As time passes and the girls grow from teenagers into womanhood, they remain connected. But the bond between them begins to show signs of stress as Marina's controlling personality suffocates Holly. As the narrative develops, it is more evident that Marina's pathetic attempts to foil Holly's happiness spring from a deep-rooted insecurity. Marina is more dependent on Holly than she would ever admit.

Rarely does one stay so closely connected with childhood friends as Holly and Marina have. But remaining best friends their whole lives has a detrimental effect on the women. Their individual identities become stifled in favor of their Harina identity. This becomes the crux of the conflict as each struggles to define themselves independently from the other. Other factors contribute the deterioration of the friendship as well. Although they share everything, both women keep a college affair with the same married professor (Kyle MacLachlan) a secret from each other until it explodes in their faces. Later, Holly begins a romantic relationship with Marina's brother Nat (Oliver Milburn), a cause of bitter jealousy for Marina who didn't want anyone to come between her and her brother.

Goldbacher infuses the narrative with classic tell-tale signs of the period. Signature '80s songs and fashion sensibilities are in full force as is the punk attitude of the '70s and the materialism of the '90s. Goldbacher guides the actors with a gentle hand, drawing nuanced performances from both women.

At certain moments, "Me Without You" can be engrossing, yet unappealing scenes of heroin consumption or boasts about the number of sexual conquests diminish the film's allure. And as the characters' manufactured problems pile up (problems created by their own selfish needs), the story drags, taking a depressing turn before abruptly turning the corner to a sunny, incongruent ending.

Due to several sexual situations with nudity, some drug abuse and recurring rough language with brief profanity, the U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops classification is A-IV -- adults, with reservations. Not rated by the Motion Picture Association of America.

(
2002
)
